text:
Tao Li: FYI I found a batch of objects in backups-bucket that are missing our `cipherstate` metadata. happened around 02:12 UTC from the uploader job. audit shows PutObject calls with no SSE header.
Samira Patel: ugh. can you paste the audit lines?
Tao Li: here — excerpt from cloud audit: ```json
{
  "protoPayload": {
    "methodName": "storage.objects.insert",
    "authenticationInfo": {
      "principalEmail": "uploader-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
    },
    "request": {
      "headers": { }
    }
  },
  "resourceName": "projects/_/buckets/backups-bucket/objects/2026-03-18/tenant123.tar.gz"
}
```
Maria Gomez: immediate action: revoke the uploader SA PutObject permission and create a short-lived grant for the expected code path. dont let more plaintext blobs in. :lock:
Jonathan K: wasn’t there an RBAC tweak last week for the uploader role? could be related.
Tao Li: yes — we added `storage.uploader` role to `uploader-sa` on 2026-03-18 01:40 UTC to unblock a throughput regression. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/commit/ab3f2e
Isabel Rivera: opened the PR diff — it also updated the bucket policy to allow `PutObject` without requiring `x-amz-server-side-encryption` header (looks like an accidental override). I’ll paste the snippet: ```yaml
- Condition: "aws:RequestHeader/x-amz-server-side-encryption": "AES256"
+ (removed)
```
Pranay: so the bucket policy change removed the enforcement gate. That explains missing cipher metadata. Which key did uploads normally use? cloud-cmk alias `alias/redwood/backups`?
Tao Li: correct — we normally require SSE-KMS with that CMK. uploader client was supposed to set `x-amz-server-side-encryption: aws:kms` and `x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id: alias/redwood/backups` but the header was absent.
oncall-sre: I’ll take lead for mitigation. plan: 1) revoke `storage.objects.create` binding for uploader-sa (samira) 2) rotate uploader service account creds if short-lived tokens used (samira) 3) run inventory to find objects missing `x-amz-meta-cipherstate` (tao) 4) mark objects for re-encryption/restore to a staging bucket then copy back with SSE-KMS (maria) 5) put a deny bucket policy that blocks PutObject without the SSE header (jonathan/isabel) 6) audit log alert + pager escalation rules (pranay).
Samira Patel: done — I removed the IAM role binding and created a temporary scoped grant in the key policy that expires in 30m.
enc-ops-bot: Incident created: INC-4502 — Cipherstate-missing objects detected in backups-bucket. Pager duty notified.
Tao Li: inventory query (aws cli) to list suspect objects: ```bash
aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket backups-bucket --prefix 2026-03-18/ --query "Contents[].{Key:Key}" | jq -r '.[] | .Key' | while read k; do aws s3api head-object --bucket backups-bucket --key "$k" --query "Metadata"; done | grep -B2 -A2 cipherstate || echo "missing"
```
Samira Patel: for immediate damage control, we should deny any PutObject operations that don't include `x-amz-server-side-encryption` via bucket policy so we don't rely on people remembering headers. policy draft: ```json
{
  "Effect": "Deny",
  "Principal": "*",
  "Action": "s3:PutObject",
  "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::backups-bucket/*",
  "Condition": {
    "Null": {
      "s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption": "true"
    }
  }
}
```
Maria Gomez: agreed. also long term we need a CI check on infra PRs that diff bucket policies and surface removal of SSE conditions.
Jonathan K: I’ll add a pre-merge policy lint that flags removals of `x-amz-server-side-encryption` conditions. assigning to infra repo owners.
Pranay: also update KMS key policy so that only principals with the `s3:PutObject` request that include correct headers can call `kms:Encrypt`. we can use `kms:ViaService` + request condition `kms:EncryptionContext:aws:s3:arn` if supported.
Isabel Rivera: made a quick script to tag objects needing re-encrypt and create a worklist: ```python
# pseudo
for obj in list_keys(prefix='2026-03-18/'):
  meta = head_object(obj)
  if 'cipherstate' not in meta:
    tag_object(obj, {'re_encrypt':'true'})
```
Tao Li: running scan now, ETA ~15m. found ~137 objects missing cipherstate so far.
Samira Patel: I started disabling uploader job runs (k8s CronJob paused) and rotated tokens.
oncall-sre: we need owners for restore: Maria lead copy/re-encrypt, Tao run validation, Jonathan get the policy changes merged, Isabel update runbook and onboarding docs, Pranay update KMS policy. Samira to follow up with audit ticket linking INC-4502.
Maria Gomez: I'll coordinate the re-encrypt window and mark maintenance in the console. we should also surface a usage report to the storage-costs team in case copies spike.
Pranay: postmortem checklist — root cause: policy drift during emergency RBAC change. Remediation: policy lint, pre-merge checks, automated bucket-level SSE enforcement, and an alert for head-object metadata anomalies.
Tao Li: quick note — for the restore we should avoid immediate key rotation unless we suspect key compromise; rotating will complicate restore. recommend re-encrypt with same CMK and then evaluate rotation on schedule.
Samira Patel: agree. creating follow-up tasks in INC-4502 with owners.
Isabel Rivera: I’ll update onboarding docs to call out required headers and add a test that uploads a tiny file and validates metadata in CI.
Jonathan K: once policy is merged, we should run a smoke copy to confirm denies work as expected.
Maria Gomez: thanks team — good catch. please add any timeline updates to the incident ticket. :eyes:
